subject: SLA-driven fleet scenarios for EHR Solutions: Private vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Natalie Chu <natalie@ehrsolutions.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPO <dpo@ehrsolutions.com>, EHR Solutions Security <security@ehrsolutions.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity ask — regulated inference for EHR workflows

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking a look — we're evaluating Redwood for a patient-data intensive inference flow that will sit behind our EHR. We have a compliance requirement to isolate PHI processing and an SLA target of 200ms 95th percentile for short clinical prompts (avg 256 tokens, peak concurrency ~40 rps).

High-level asks:
- Can you outline the trade-offs between a Private (VPC/on‑prem control plane) and a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) deployment for us?
- We need a rough GPU-sizing estimate and an explanation of burst behavior and fallback policies (if Dedicated capacity is saturated).
- Procurement timeline: we may need pricing and a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to move procurement in Q3.

Attached is a small sample of our request traces (sensitive fields redacted). Appreciate a pragmatic recommendation — we prefer predictable latency and data isolation but want to understand cost delta and operational lift.

-Natalie
Lead Architect, EHR Solutions
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Chu <natalie@ehrsolutions.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — regulated inference for EHR workflows

Hi Natalie — thanks for the trace sample and context. Quick confirmation: the 200ms P95 is the external SLA you want Redwood to meet from request ingress to token emission, correct? Also confirming average sequence length ~256 tokens, peak 40 rps, with occasional spikes to 75 rps for short windows.

I'll sketch two vetted scenarios and a recommended pilot path. To produce a more accurate GPU count I need:
- Typical request length distribution (p50/p90/p99 token counts)
- Percentage of requests that require function/tool calls or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — these affect KV cache hit behavior
- Acceptable warm-up time for new model versions (can you tolerate a few minutes of degraded latency during rollouts?)

In the meantime, high level guidance:
- Private: best for maximal control (networking, KMS/HSM, audit surface). Higher ops & procurement (on‑prem or VPC egress) but can provide near-zero external data path risk. Good if DPO requires customer-controlled key material.
- Dedicated: fast procurement, predictable committed throughput, built-in autoscaling and burst. We can provision an isolated GPU pool per account with strict tenancy and networking. If you need cryptographic separation (customer HSM), Private is easier.

I'll loop in Sales Ops for MAP and pricing once we lock the workload profile. Attaching a short checklist of follow-up items.

—Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Natalie Chu <natalie@ehrsolutions.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — regulated inference for EHR workflows

Marcus — thanks. Quick answers and an updated trace attached (ehr_workload_sample.csv):
- token distribution in the sample: p50=180, p90=420, p99=900 (most are short).
- ~18% of requests trigger an external retrieval step (RAG).
- Rollouts: we need canary windows but can tolerate up to 10 minutes of longer tails during a deploy.
- Procurement: procurement wants a MAP and a draft SOW by end of June to hit a July purchase order.

Let me know if you need anything else (SOC2 evidence would smooth internal security review).

Regards,
Natalie
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: EHR Solutions — sizing scenarios for Q3 MAP

Team — forwarding Natalie's numbers. Drafted two operational scenarios (quick back-of-envelope, include assumptions):

Assumptions from sample: p90=420 tokens, p99 spikes to 900, avg session mixes RAG (18%). Model candidate: a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit with KV cache enabled. We aim for ~200ms P95 for short prompts.

Scenario A — Dedicated isolated pool (recommended if customer prefers Redwood-managed with strict tenancy):
- Steady baseline (40 rps at p90): ~6 A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (continuous batching, KV cache hit rate ~70%)
- Buffer for spikes / burst: additional 2 GPUs in warm standby => total reserved 8 GPUs
- Autoscaling: policy to allow short bursts up to +50% using burst-capacity credits for 10m windows; fallback route to a slightly smaller model variant with degraded P95 (~350ms) if sustained saturation >5m.
- Estimated monthly committed cost delta vs. hosted: ~x4 (due to reserved capacity & isolation overhead).

Scenario B — Private VPC deployment (customer-managed control plane or on‑prem agent):
- For same throughput target, similar GPU count (6 active + 2 warm) — but network egress constraints and on‑prem procurement timelines push TTM out by 6–10 weeks.
- Ops: customer responsible for KMS/HSM, maintenance windows. Potential cost reductions over long-term if they amortize hardware (buy vs rent).

Risk and ops notes:
- RAG paths increase per-request latency variance; recommend increasing cache TTLs where safe and pre‑warm retrieval models when possible.
- If they require HSM-backed encryption of model keys, Private is preferred. Dedicated can support customer-managed keys in some cases but needs legal + infra approvals.

Next steps I propose:
1) Draft MAP + SOW stub for both scenarios (I can lead).
2) Price band for 6 vs 8 GPU reservation + burst credits (Sales Ops: priyom, can you issue a target price range we can present?).
3) Security pack: attach SOC2 summary & our network isolation spec. Mina — please flag any compliance gaps for the MAP.

Thanks — I'll convert this into a single-page decision memo to send back to Natalie.

—Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Chu <natalie@ehrsolutions.com>
Cc: DPO <dpo@ehrsolutions.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Recommendation and MAP draft — EHR Solutions dedicated vs private path

Hi Natalie — thanks for the trace and patience. Based on your p90/p99 distribution and RAG fraction, here is our pragmatic recommendation and how we suggest progressing to a July PO.

Executive recommendation (short):
- Pilot on Dedicated isolated pool (8 reserved GPUs: 6 active + 2 warm) for fast time-to-value and predictable latency. This meets your 200ms P95 target in most pre‑production tests and lets us move quickly on MAP/pricing.
- Parallel due-diligence track for Private (VPC or on‑prem) if DPO decides they need full KMS/HSM control before long-term commit. Private is mechanically similar sizing but will add 6–10 weeks to TTM.

Rationale summary:
- Dedicated gives predictable throughput and simpler procurement (monthly commitment) enabling you to hit an aggressive Q3 rollout.
- Private makes sense for cryptographic separation or policy reasons — choose if procurement can accept longer lead time and CAPEX/op-ex tradeoffs.

Attachments included: MAP_ehrsolutions_draft.md (mutual action plan with milestones), SOC2_summary_2026.pdf (security evidence), ehr_workload_sample.csv (your sample).

Proposed next steps (to hit PO in July):
1) Confirm pilot target date (we recommend 2027-07-11 for a 2-week pilot).
2) PRIO: I need a confirmation of the procurement decision owner and PO path.
3) Sales Ops (cc'd priyom) will send a price band for the 8 GPU reserved pool + burst credits and a separate indicative T&M for the Private onboarding.
4) Sign MAP + SOW stub (I attached the draft).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the MAP and the performance tuning knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
